pointers.sentence: `empty` is a bare `object()` (`django/utils/functional.py:empty`).
`LazyObject.__init__` puts it in `_wrapped`; `LazyObject._setup` raises `NotImplementedError`, and a subclass writes it to assign the object to `_wrapped` (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject`).

`LazyObject.__setattr__` writes `_wrapped` into the proxy's own `__dict__` and, for any other name, sets the object up and sets the attribute on it; `LazyObject.__delattr__` refuses `_wrapped` with `TypeError` and deletes anything else from the object (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__setattr__`, `django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__delattr__`).

`LazyObject.__setattr__` writes `_wrapped` into the proxy's own `__dict__` and, for any other name, sets the object up and sets the attribute on it; `LazyObject.__delattr__` refuses `_wrapped` with `TypeError` and deletes anything else from the object (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__setattr__`, `django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__delattr__`).

`new_method_proxy` makes every forwarding method of `LazyObject` but `__setattr__` and `__delattr__`, as a function that takes the proxy, calls `_setup` if `_wrapped` is `empty`, calls the given function on the wrapped object, and is marked `_mask_wrapped = False` (`django/utils/functional.py:new_method_proxy`).

The special methods are class attributes made the same way: `__str__`, `__bytes__`, `__bool__`, `__dir__`, `__hash__`, `__eq__`, `__ne__`, `__lt__`, `__gt__`, `__getitem__`, `__setitem__`, `__delitem__`, `__iter__`, `__len__` and `__contains__` (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject`).

`LazyObject.__getattribute__`, which every attribute read passes through, raises `AttributeError` for what the ordinary lookup finds marked `_mask_wrapped = False`, so that, as its comment says, `__getattr__` answers from the wrapped object (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__getattribute__`):

`__class__` is forwarded, as a property made by `new_method_proxy`, because, the comment says, objects that care about the class, in equality tests above all, must see the wrapped one (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject`).

`LazyObject.__reduce__` sets the object up and has pickle write `unpickle_lazyobject` with the wrapped object as its argument, a function that returns its argument (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__reduce__`).

The migration serializer reads a lazy object's value from the same arguments ([Serializing values: `serializer_factory` and `deconstruct`](../migrations/serializer.md)) (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:serializer_factory`).

`LazyObject.__copy__` and `LazyObject.__deepcopy__` copy the wrapper while it is empty, by `type(self)` (not `__class__`, which the comment notes is proxied), and after setup the wrapped object, so that copy is not lazy (`django/utils/functional.py:LazyObject.__copy__`).

`SimpleLazyObject.__init__` writes the function straight into the instance's `__dict__` as `"_setupfunc"`, where an assignment would have gone through `__setattr__` to the wrapped object; `SimpleLazyObject._setup` calls it and stores the result (`django/utils/functional.py:SimpleLazyObject`).

A function that is a bound method of the proxy is shown only by its name, to avoid recursion, as the comment says: a bound method's repr holds its object's, and with the check removed a run raised `RecursionError` (`django/utils/functional.py:SimpleLazyObject.__repr__`).
